question.text: Two persons <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> perform same amount of work in moving a body through a certain distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> with application of forces acting at angles <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the direction of displacement respectively. The ratio of force applied by person <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> to the force applied by person <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mfrac><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _________.

solution.text: Given, W1=W2 and, we know that work done is a scalar quantity it means, F1Scos45°=F2Scos60°⇒F1F2=12=1x⇒x=2.
